claims.content: Customer
The Customer clicks the 'QuickBid Now' button to place a single bid on an auction item, or selects an amount and clicks the 'Place SmartBid' or 'Place Single Bid' button.
The Customer remains on the Product Details Page of the auction item after the bid is placed, rather than being redirected to a confirmation or checkout page.
The system records the bid in the Item Bid History table with a timestamp precise to 1/100th of a second.
The Item Bid History table on the Product Details Page updates to display the new bid entry with the bidder's Name, Amount, Date Placed, and SmartBid User status.
The system updates the 'Current High Bid' dynamically for all items without requiring a page refresh.
The Customer's Watch List data for the item is updated to show the new Current High Bid, Total Bids, Last Bid Time, and Ending Time.

missing_aspects: Evidence EC-PO-009 confirms the recording of Name, Amount, Date Placed, and SmartBid User status. Evidence EC-PO-005 confirms the 1/100th of a second precision requirement for all bids. However, neither card explicitly states that the 'Item Bid History table' specifically displays this level of precision (mockup shows MM:SS), nor does EC-PO-005 explicitly link the precision requirement to the history table record itself versus the backend processing.

Evidence EC-PO-011 describes the static display capabilities of the 'My Watch List' page (showing columns for these values). It does not explicitly state that placing a bid triggers an immediate update to this specific view or that the user is viewing this list at the moment of the postcondition.

claims.content: The Customer is signed in to the system; if not signed in, the user is redirected to the sign-in page before a bid can be placed.
The signed-in Customer's account contains the required minimum information needed to place a bid.
The Customer has agreed to be bound by the Terms of Use Agreement, as required to participate in auctions.

missing_aspects: Evidence EC-PC-003 describes the system's response (returning the user to the product details page) when the user lacks the required minimum information. It does not explicitly state that possessing this information is a precondition for placing a bid, though it implies it. The claim should reflect the source text's focus on the check and the consequence of failure.

claims.content: At the sign-in check, if the Customer is not signed in when attempting to place a bid (e.g., clicking the QuickBid button or anywhere within the product module), the system takes the Customer to the sign-in page; after the Customer completes the sign-in process, the system delivers the Customer to the Product Details page. Exit: return to the Product Details page.
At the sign-in check, if the Customer is not signed in when clicking the QuickBid button, the Customer is prompted to sign in and is then returned to the catalog page.

Minimum-information recovery: when the Customer has the required minimum information required to bid, the system returns the Customer to the Product Details page of the item they initially tried to bid on.
At the bid-eligibility check, if the Customer has unresolved (i.e., unpaid) auction winnings greater than 7 days old, the system does not allow the Customer to bid.

At the bid-eligibility check, if the Customer is subject to the escalation policy (failing to pay more than three times in a twelve-month period, unless less than 10% of total winnings), the Customer cannot bid again until a Customer Service Representative removes the account from Review Status.
At the bid confirmation popup dialog, if the Customer clicks the 'CANCEL' button, the Customer cancels the bid confirmation.

missing_aspects: Immediate system behavior when the Customer is found to lack the required minimum information at the moment of attempting to place a bid; the available evidence only documents the return to the Product Details page once the information is present.

Post-cancellation outcome after the Customer clicks CANCEL in the bid confirmation popup (e.g., whether the Customer is returned to the Product Details page or the use case terminates without placing the bid).
How the Customer regains the ability to bid after being blocked for unresolved unpaid auction winnings greater than 7 days old.

claims.content: The Customer selects an amount and clicks the 'Place SmartBid' or 'Place Single Bid' button, or clicks the 'QuickBid Now' button to place a single bid.
The system displays a 'Bid Confirmation Pop-up' stating the bid amount, type, and payment method (e.g., credit card ending), with 'Yes, Place [Type] Bid' and 'Cancel' buttons.
The Customer confirms the bid by clicking 'Yes, Place SmartBid' (or the equivalent for the selected bid type).
The system processes the bid, and the Customer remains on the Product Details Page.
The system records the bid in the 'Item Bid History' table with the bidder's Name, Amount, Date Placed, and SmartBid User status, and records the bid time to 1/100th of a second.
The system updates the 'Current High Bid' dynamically for all items without requiring a page refresh.
The system updates the Customer's watch list record for the item to show the new Current High Bid, Total Bids, Last Bid Time, and Ending Time.

Diverges from Step 1: instead of selecting an amount on the auction item's Product Details page, the Customer places a bid directly from a listing page by clicking the 'QuickBid' button — located under the item's price and timer in the catalog view, or next to the item in the Category Page List View.

Diverges from Step 1: instead of selecting a bid amount from the 'Your SmartBid' or 'Your Single Bid' dropdowns, the Customer initiates a bid by clicking the 'QuickBid Now' button, which uses the value in the 'QuickBid Amount' field.
Diverges from Step 1: the Customer accesses bidding options via the 'SmartBid' button located on the Category Page List View.

Diverges from Step 4: when overtime bidding is ON and a bid is placed within the time extension window (e.g., five seconds before scheduled end), the system automatically extends the auction by the configured duration (e.g., 20 seconds); if another bid is placed during the extension, it extends again for the same duration.

missing_aspects: Rejoin point into the main flow for the listing-view QuickBid and Category-Page SmartBid alternatives (e.g., whether the Step 2 bid confirmation pop-up is shown or bypassed) is not documented.
Evidence confirms the existence of the 'SmartBid' button on the list view but does not explicitly state that it is used to initiate a bid (as opposed to accessing options).

inconsistency_hints: The Trigger includes two valid initiating actions: clicking 'QuickBid Now' to place a single bid, or selecting an amount and clicking 'Place SmartBid'/'Place Single Bid'. Main Flow step 1 only continues the amount-selection variant, so the QuickBid Now path has no matching continuation and the flow appears to restart as a different scenario.
